pois.s:
The Ayles Ice Shelf was one of six major ice shelves in Canada, all on the north coast of Ellesmere Island, Nunavut. The ice shelf broke off from the coast on August 13, 2005, forming a giant ice island 37 metres (121 feet) thick and measuring around 14 by 5 kilometres (8.7 by 3.1 miles) in size (approximately 55 square kilometres (21 square miles) in area or 2.6 cubic kilometres (0.62 cubic miles) in volume). The oldest ice in the ice shelf is believed to be over 3,000 years old. The ice shelf was at (82°52′N 80°30′W), approximately 800 km (500 mi) south of the North Pole.

The Ayles Ice Shelf, like the nearby Mount Ayles, was named for the Arctic explorer, Adam Ayles, who served as the chief petty officer of HMS Alert under George Nares in the British Arctic Expedition.
